about: The timeline as rows: one per signal, with who published it (publisher) where the source has a URL. Built by tools/graph-build.mjs from the incident's JSON; every row carries label, source, read and origin. Not a warning service.

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: IPMA expects the storm earlier, Wednesday morning; Lisbon among the hardest hit; avoid unnecessary travel (Lusa)

rows.label: fact
rows.text: The government declares an alert situation for the mainland on Wednesday, 00:00 to 23:59: schools and non-essential public services close; outdoor events suspended
rows.via: portugal.gov.pt (page dated 12:10; S41 updated with it at 17:27), read by weather@

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Web Summit's organisers following the alerts with ANEPC and PSP; no sign yet of cancelling Wednesday
rows.via: Jornal de Negócios, live; via social.watch@PrompTugal.dinis

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Lisbon's mayor: "Tudo indica que a Web Summit não poderá funcionar amanhã"; the decision is the Interior Ministry's and the organisers'

rows.label: fact
rows.text: IPMA red warning for wind, Lisbon district, Wednesday 12:00 to 21:00 (first read by the newsroom)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Web Summit in doubt; Tagus bridges limited to 60 km/h; Lisbon tunnels closed from midnight; Metro keeps running

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: the storm leaves Web Summit with a thin audience
rows.via: Jornal de Negócios, live; via social.watch@PrompTugal.dinis

rows.label: fact
rows.text: Dinis: the storm is our case study (a dynamic team, the decision graph)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: water enters a pavilion between halls 4 and 5; participants leave early
rows.via: Jornal de Negócios, live; via social.watch@PrompTugal.dinis

rows.label: fact
rows.text: IPMA raises Lisbon's rain warning to red, Wednesday 12:00 to 18:00
rows.via: IPMA open data, read by weather@

rows.label: fact
rows.text: Web Summit: no change to Wednesday's programme announced on its homepage or news page

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: the government recommends suspending Web Summit on Wednesday; the decision rests with the organisers
rows.via: Jornal de Negócios, live; via social.watch@PrompTugal.dinis

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: (unofficial) an attendee post says the event is "most likely" closed tomorrow; speculation, not an announcement

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: no organiser statement after the government's recommendation (the live blog's last update read)
rows.via: Jornal de Negócios, live; via social.watch@PrompTugal.dinis

rows.label: fact
rows.text: Incident declared (P1, run on account A) at Dinis's word

rows.label: fact
rows.text: Vicky's weather desk full check: IPMA's two red warnings for Lisbon unchanged since 17:42 (wind 12:00 to 21:00, rain 12:00 to 18:00); no Web Summit change

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Organisers checked again: no decision on Wednesday; their last line is still "assessing with ANEPC and PSP"

rows.label: fact
rows.text: Lead handed over: incident.conductor@web-summit.dinis takes the lead of WS-214 from conductor@web-summit.dinis, at Dinis's word (team/incidents/BRIEF.md); the timeline is kept newest first from here

rows.label: fact
rows.text: No Web Summit decision on Wednesday found (organiser channels readable without a login)

rows.label: fact
rows.text: No Web Summit decision on Wednesday: websummit.com (home, /news/, sitemap), its official Bluesky (last post 17:36, "wrap on Day 1") and Jornal de Negócios live (last entry 18:24)

rows.label: hypothesis
rows.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, labelled): worst window Wed 12:00 to 18:00, peak most likely ~15:00 to 19:00 around the wind's swing to north-west, easing but dangerous to 21:00; red wind was known ~27.5 h ahead; confidence medium on the window, low on the peak
rows.via: data/weather/analysis.md (from IPMA warnings, communiqué no. 2, LPPT TAF, IPMA model, read 19:01)

rows.label: fact
rows.text: PRIMARY: Web Summit's own page, "Important event update": "Day 2 (Wednesday, November 11th) will not take place"; "Web Summit aims to proceed with Day 3 (Thursday, November 12) as planned, following the passing of Storm Charles"; reasons: tidal flooding, disruption to public transport, high winds on external structures; "Web Summit will communicate directly with those impacted". Under /blog/web-summit/, not in the news list; we did not watch that path
rows.via: websummit.com; (page data: published 19:09:00, modified 19:25:44; found by social.watch@PrompTugal.dinis, read at source by the lead 20:58)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: DECISION: Web Summit's Day 2, Wednesday 11 November, will not take place. The government "formally advised" it (tidal flooding, public transport, high winds on external structures), after talks with the government, ANEPC and PSP; Day 3, Thursday 12 November, aimed to go ahead as planned
rows.via: Web Summit's email to attendees (no public URL), relayed by weather@PrompTugal.vicky (b23e846, 19:48) and conductor@web-summit.dinis (19:52)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Web Summit closed on Wednesday after talks with the government, ANEPC and PSP; the mayor calls it the most sensible decision

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Public: "Após recomendação do Governo, Paddy suspende Web Summit na quarta-feira"; the organisers quoted: the government "informou formalmente a Web Summit" of the risks
rows.via: Jornal de Negócios, live, 19:42; read 19:52 by incident.conductor@ (also by social.watch@ at 19:53)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: organisers cancel all of Wednesday's activities (coastal flooding, wind on outdoor structures, transport), after coordinating with the authorities
rows.via: Diário de Notícias, live; via social.watch@PrompTugal.dinis (sweep 2)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: organisers will hold Thursday "conforme planeado, após a passagem da tempestade Charles"; people affected will be contacted directly

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Thursday resumes "if the weather allows" (DN's wording; RTP's "as planned, after the storm"; the organisers' own page: "aims to proceed")

rows.label: fact
rows.text: Checked by the lead: websummit.com home and news list carry no notice of Day 2 (the notice was already up at /blog/web-summit/ since 19:09, a path we did not check)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: organisers will contact those affected directly; not said whether Wednesday's programme is cancelled or moved (N6 still open)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: the cancellation in the international press (PT and EN); coast and riverside access prohibited Wednesday; nothing on refunds or PITCH

rows.label: fact
rows.text: The incident moves to its own site: https://storm-charles.promptugal.news (this repository); first push to served 23 s (v0.1.2), against 3 to 10 minutes on web-summit.sgit.ai

rows.label: hypothesis
rows.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, labelled): IPMA's hourly model changed its values (same 07:55 stamp): Wednesday's strongest mean wind now 23 km/h at 20:00 (was 49 at 18:00); the swing to north 18:00; peak most likely 17:00 to 20:00 (was 15:00 to 19:00); worst window 12:00 to 18:00 and end 21:00 unchanged; IPMA's red warnings unchanged and outrank one model

rows.label: fact
rows.text: Web Summit's blog listing shows the update post modified 20:06; its text unchanged on Day 2 and Day 3 ("aims to proceed")

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: a speaker says in public that Day 2 is cancelled and his talks and press conference stay on Thursday (the first sign that Thursday's programme holds for some speakers)
rows.via: Jon S. von Tetzchner on Mastodon; via social.watch@ (sweep 4)

rows.label: fact
rows.text: No further statement from Web Summit (social.watch@'s sweep 4); still open: Wednesday's talks, the PITCH semi-final (when it was set is in conflict: Wednesday 17:00 in social.watch@'s summary, unsourced there; Thursday in Tech Times' preview of 9 Nov), side events (Web Summit's own Night Summit still listed for Wednesday 18:00 to 00:00, no notice, 22:05), tickets

rows.label: fact
rows.text: The first airport TAF covering Thursday (issued 23:00) is weaker than 17:00's: Wed 09:00 to 16:00 at times 30 kt gusting 45 (83 km/h); 30% chance (was 40%) of 58 kt thunderstorm gusts 10:00 to 18:00; west 12 kt from 18:00 to 20:00; Thursday 00:00 to 06:00 west 12 kt, no gusts. IPMA's red warnings unchanged
rows.via: LPPT TAF (IPMA, via NOAA's Aviation Weather), data/weather/airport.json (incident.meteorologist@, a63ac9696)

rows.label: hypothesis
rows.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, labelled): the TAF's peak (09:00 to 16:00) and IPMA's model peak (19:00 to 20:00) disagree, so the peak is widened back to 12:00 to 18:00; end 21:00; Thursday morning behind the storm, medium confidence; a weaker airport forecast is not a downgrade of IPMA's warning
